_meta.frame: Persepolis grid (x grid-east, y grid-north, metres), origin Apadana OSM centroid 29.9351174N 52.8894969E, grid north 341 deg true. xy from pyproj tmerc + rotate (tools/osm_to_grid.py convention; the local approximation in src/core/geo.ts differs by <2 m at 6 km and ~80 m at 40 km).
_meta.tiers: tier = lowest of existence and position; every scholarly source was seen only as a web-search extract (BLOCKERS B6), so existence is capped at B; positions are C unless a dataset coordinate exists.
_meta.fields: id, kind, name, tier, src (keys in sources.json), note, date_range, present_467 (true / false / null = not placed), xy or polygon or polyline (grid m), latlon, unc_m (1-sigma position uncertainty, m)
_meta.layout_warning: Layout of the town, housing, storehouses and stables is reconstruction (C). Only Tol-e Ajori (size), Persepolis West Area B (activity), Takht-e Rustam (size) and the existence of garden zones, a 1 ha official building and a Pulvar canal are sourced.

density.town_note: 3,000-6,000 is PEOPLE.md section 3e's first-pass figure; PEOPLE.md P5.6 replaces it with 5,000-10,000 (working value 7,000; Q-038), and the build has 1,456 homes for 7,968 people (town_plots.json) holding 7,776 (D-081, seed 1). See research/SETTLEMENT.md section 3 (D-228).

garden_planting.src: SAEIDI2021 via research/_climate_C.md (pollen: Olea, Punica, Platanus, cypress with Achaemenid arboriculture, B); IR-FOODAG (PF fruits, B)
garden_planting.layout: rectilinear beds divided by stone-lined or earthen channels, by analogy with Pasargadae (B analogy, C here)

not_placed: storehouses: PF stores exist, no excavated store outside the Terrace. The Phase 6 build places ONE storehouse as C (town_elements town_stores; D-043)
stables: horse rations in PF (POTTS2023); no stable excavated. The Phase 6 build places ONE state stable as C (town_elements town_stables; D-043)
qanats (no archaeologically dated Achaemenid qanat; QANAT-WH2018) - wells and river canals only
_meta.town_elements: Reconstruction rows (Phase 6 build): every generated plot, fitting and prop names one of these rows (tier, sources, basis) and a present feature (in_feature). tools/lint_chrono.ts checks them fail-closed.

features.name: Tol-e Ajori gate (Bagh-e Firuzi)
features.note: Mud brick with baked and glazed brick facing; plan modelled on the inner section of Babylon's Ishtar Gate but larger; two entrance corridors (TOLAJORI2017, SX, B). Size 39.07 m NW-SE x 29.05 m NE-SW (B). Height ~12 m and "30-40 m wide" are press figures (C). Glazed relief bricks copy the Babylonian panels (bulls, dragons) "down to the smallest detail" (B). Position: "3.5 km NW" (AJORI-BRICK2018), "3 km" (press), "almost 3.5 km W/NW, S side of the Pulvar" (DASHTESTAN2021): placed 3.3 km at 295 deg true, S of the modern Pulvar (C, +-700 m). State in 467 unknown: the 2014 report traces it "from construction to destruction" but the date of destruction was not retrieved (Q-004, Q-051). Working value: standing, old and unrepaired (C).
features.axis_note: long side NW-SE, WNW-ESE at 110/290 deg true; the passage runs along the long axis through corridors on the short sides (plan_2026, B). Superseded: 'passage direction not retrieved (C: NE-SW)'.

plan_2026.benches: low benches along the inner room walls
plan_2026.corridors: two entrance corridors, on the NW and SE short sides (so the passage runs along the long axis)
plan_2026.motifs: aurochs and mushhushshu glazed relief bricks copied from the Babylonian panels; originally a blue ground, the surviving colours paler
plan_2026.access: SX (search extracts of the 2017 report abstract and of Wikipedia 'Ishtar Gate', 2026-09-23)
plan_2026.note: "rectangular plan ... 39.07 m (NW-SE) x 29.05 m (NE-SW), oriented from WNW to ESE, with a 20 deg shift to N from the E-W axis. Its outer perimeter is formed by a massive wall 10.47 m thick, which encloses a rather limited inner room (w. 8.00 m, l. 14.36 m) with low benches along its walls and accessed by two corridors on the NW and SE short sides" (abstract as quoted by the search engine). Supersedes the earlier C guess of a NE-SW passage (D-042).

features.name: Bagh-e Firuzi palace-and-garden zone
features.note: Very low-density elite/royal occupation set in large green spaces with Achaemenid garden complexes (GONDET2009, SX, B); "important urban zone ... 3.5 km W/NW ... S side of the Pulvar" (DASHTESTAN2021, B). Column bases and foundations beyond the gate (press, C). Extent is reconstructed (C): 1.7 x 1.5 km around the gate, N edge kept S of the modern Pulvar.

features.name: Persepolis West (Sumner's Firuzi mounds; lower town)
features.note: Low mounds W of the Terrace with dense surface material (Sumner, via DASHTESTAN2021/GONDET2009); geophysics: strong magnetism read as kilns and craft activity, and the levelled remains of a settlement with mud-brick structures (B). Geomagnetic survey 50 ha in 23 areas; 11 trial trenches 2008-09 (PW2017, B). Many geomagnetic plans are post-Achaemenid (PW2017 review, B). Barrington Atlas "Firuzi 2 / Matezzish? / Humadeshu? / Uvadaichaya?" (settlement, Classical = 550-330 BCE) is this cluster; the BA point itself is map-scale (C). Extent reconstructed (C).

features.name: Persepolis West Area A (strong geomagnetic anomalies)
features.note: Area A lay W of the modern Persepolis parking lot (PW2017, B). Placed 200 m W of the parking centroid (C, +-200 m). Findings in Area A not retrieved.

features.name: Persepolis West Area B craft zone: kiln, bone pits, pigment workshop
features.note: Area B 500 m W of Area A (PW2017, B). A kiln and industrial remains "of possible Achaemenid date"; pits full of bone fragments, read as raw material for fluorapatite used to whiten the grey limestone of the Terrace (B). Pigment lumps: azurite, malachite, Egyptian blue, glauconite, red and yellow ochre (haematite, magnetite, goethite); a bronze scrap with an Egyptian-blue crust and diopside suggest Egyptian blue was made here; palette matches the Terrace palaces (PW-PIGMENT2021, B). Position C (+-250 m); activity B; date in 467 C (possible Achaemenid). Tier C (D-228): activity and existence B, position C (+-250 m, placed 500 m W of a placed Area A); the file's rule is tier = the lower of existence and position.
crafts: pigment making (Egyptian blue, ochres, malachite, azurite)

features.name: Persepolis West Area C: garden (ditch grid + fence wall)
features.note: A grid of ditches with a fencing wall, read as a garden (B). Position not retrieved: placed in the W part of Persepolis West (C, +-600 m).

blocklist_ok.signage: "fence wall" is the excavated Achaemenid garden enclosure wall (PW2017), not a modern fence

features.name: ~1 ha building N of the "Frataraka" complex
features.note: Geophysics and pedestrian survey 2012-14 in the fields N of the Terrace revealed part of an almost 1 ha building; features suggest an Achaemenid date and an official function (B existence). Position C (+-300 m), size ~100 x 100 m (C).

blocklist_ok.frataraka: the name only locates this Achaemenid building N of the post-Achaemenid complex, which itself is absent

features.name: "Frataraka" complex (pedestal temple)
features.note: Post-Achaemenid by Callieri (brick sizes, column-base types, pedestal style) (SX, B). ABSENT in 467. Position C (N of the Terrace). Tier C (D-228): the post-Achaemenid dating that makes it absent is B, its position C (+-250 m, N of the Terrace); the file's rule is tier = the lower of existence and position.

features.name: Takht-e Rustam (unfinished stepped platform)
features.note: Local stone, about 12.5 x 12.5 m, base for a higher structure; resembles the lower tiers of Cyrus' tomb; suggested tomb of Cambyses (LIVIUS-TR, SX: B for size, C for attribution). "Two kilometers south of Naqsh-e Rustam", on the road from Naqsh-e Rustam to Naqsh-e Rajab: placed 2 km from Naqsh-e Rustam toward Naqsh-e Rajab (C, +-400 m). CONFLICT: the Barrington/DARMC point for "Dasht-i Gohar/Takht-i Rustam" lies 0.8 km S of the Terrace (accuracy 10 km, map-scale) (Q-048).

features.name: Dasht-e Gohar palace-and-garden zone
features.note: Low-density elite/royal occupation with Achaemenid garden complexes (GONDET2009, B); a hypostyle hall reburied behind the Takht-e Rustam platform (search extract, C); Barrington "settlement", Classical (B). Extent C.

features.name: Kuh-e Rahmat canal (Pulvar to Persepolis)
features.note: "The 4-km canal began at the Pulvar and followed a steep, but declining, slope toward Persepolis"; a small dam and a network of canals and gutters, with an entrance reservoir (MAYS2010, SX, B/C: engineering overview). "Kuh-e Rahmat canal" is on the map of Achaemenid hydrological traces (BOUCHARLAT2012, SX, B) and "Rahmat Mountain Canal" among Kur-basin structures (KURHYDRO2024, B). Course C: from the modern Pulvar at ~1626 m (DEM mid ring) along the NW foot of Kuh-e Rahmat to the Terrace N side (~1616 m); ~5.4 km, mean fall ~0.2 %. Width 2 m, depth 0.8 m (C).

features.name: Lower town S/SW of the Terrace (Matezziš?)
features.note: Matezziš is identified with sites in the plain adjacent to Persepolis (DASHTESTAN2021, B); the settled zone spans ~20 km2 around the Terrace but at very low density (GONDET2009, B). No excavated houses: housing form (mud-brick courtyard houses with flat roofs) is by regional analogy (C). Population 3,000-6,000 in the town and palace zone with the court absent (PEOPLE.md, C).

features.name: Road Terrace - Naqsh-e Rajab gap - Takht-e Rustam - Naqsh-e Rustam
features.note: A road "from Naqš-e Rustam to Naqš-e Rajab" passing Takht-e Rustam is stated by Livius (modern road, SX). Ancient course C; unpaved earth, 6-8 m (C). Crosses the Pulvar (ford or bridge, C).

blocklist_ok.later-sites-plain: the road passes the natural Naqsh-e Rajab gap; the Sasanian reliefs there stay absent (nr_sasanian, naqsh_e_rajab)

features.name: Road Persepolis - Pulvar valley - Sivand - Tang-e Bulaghi - Pasargadae
features.note: Persepolis and Pasargadae (Batrakataš) are ~40 km apart and linked by the Pulvar valley (Pleiades Pulvar: "flows near Pasargadae and through the Bolaghi gorge"). Course reconstructed along the modern Pulvar (C). Sivand quarry (Classical) lies near it.

features.name: Royal road toward Susa (leaves the plain W/NW)
features.note: The PF travel texts document the Susa-Persepolis road (23 stages, ~552 km in one summary) through the Fahliyan area (ROYALROAD-GIS, SX, B). Sumner records "a paved road" and parts of the Royal Road in the plain (B; location not retrieved). Course here C: along the S bank of the Pulvar past Persepolis West and Tol-e Ajori, crossing the Kur near the Pulvar confluence, then NW toward Kamfiruz.

features.name: Road S across the plain to the Kur crossing near Tukrash? and on to Tirazziš (Shiraz)
features.note: Tirazziš (Shiraz) is a PF toponym (Pleiades 922706, B); Tukrash? (Sumner) lies at the Kur 20 km S (B). Course C.

features.name: Way-station at the Kur crossing (royal road)
features.note: PF travel rations imply stations roughly a day apart; the first station W of Persepolis is not identified (C placement at the Kur crossing, ~12 km). Form: walled court with store and stable (C, analogy with Jinjun/Qaleh-ye Kali way-stations, B).

features.name: Akhor Rostam rock-cut burial niches
features.note: Vanden Berghe dated the niches to the Achaemenid period (IR-ARCH2, SX); Barrington/Pleiades list the cemetery as Roman/Late Antique (FT). Conflict (Q-049): present_467 uncertain, modelled as present (C). BA point accuracy 10 km (C).
features.build_note: Not built in Phase 6: rock-cut niches need a rock face and none lies within 1 km of the map-scale point (DEM check; nearest steep rock ~3 km E/NE). Nothing is invented in its place (Q-085).

features.name: "Spring Cemetery" near Persepolis
features.note: Extended burials in slipper coffins, simple pottery; late 4th c. BCE or later: ABSENT in 467. Position not retrieved.

features.name: Rock-cut tombs of private people near Persepolis (Herzfeld)
features.note: Cut into vertical rock or boulders, or into horizontal rock, closed by large slabs (SX, B existence); dates and positions not retrieved: not placed.

features.name: open-air sacred precinct at the foot of Kuh-e Rahmat (reconstructed)
features.note: D-209: where the magi keep a fire and the lan and other offerings are made. Forms B (the Pasargadae plinths; the Naqsh-e Rustam stepped altar); place, size and use C. No temple, shrine or statue (Herodotus 1.131, read: not their custom; none excavated; temple cults from Artaxerxes II). Placed on the level bench (slope ~5 %) at the mountain's foot 180 m S of the Terrace, 10 m above the plain, clear of the town, roads and canal

features.name: burial ground of the town (reconstructed)
features.note: D-209: the dead are coated in wax and buried in the earth (Herodotus 1.140, read, B claim). No burial ground of 467 is located (section 6): placed C on dry untilled ground at the foot of Kuh-e Rahmat, 1.1 km S of the Terrace and 250 m E of the lower town; low earth mounds, some with field stones. No exposure platform (not attested for 467; never shown)

town_elements.name: courtyard houses of the town quarters
town_elements.note: House type after the first-millennium Babylonian courtyard house (BAKER2014 with Reuther 1926 on the Merkes quarter of Babylon, search extracts: B for the analogue): a court with rooms on two to four sides, one street door into a vestibule set to block the view in, blind alleys. Babylon was inside the empire and lived in through the Achaemenid period. Plot sizes (8-16 x 10-20 m), room depths (3-4 m), roof heights (3.1-3.6 m) and capacities (13 m2 of rooms per person) are C. No house has been excavated at Persepolis.

town_elements.name: streets, lanes, blind alleys and small squares
town_elements.note: Generated maze: through streets 4 m with jogs, lanes 3 m and alleys 2 m branching until no ground lies more than 16 m from a lane (C). Babylon Merkes: wide and narrow streets, blind alleys giving access to houses (B analogue).

town_elements.name: craft workshops (treasury metal, wood and textile work; bakeries, breweries, potters)
town_elements.note: Crafts B: PT craftsmen include woodworkers, goldsmiths and stonecutters (IR-TREAS); treasury staff handle wood, carpentry supplies, precious metals and probably textiles (HENK2023); >= 1,348 employed in the treasury in 467, mostly in town workshops (LIVIUS-TREAS; split C, Q-031); PF 40 'He made beer' (A, Darius-era). Workshop places, share (5-10 % of plots) and fittings (forges, looms, ovens, querns, vats, kilns) C.

town_elements.name: back yards and walled yards
town_elements.note: ground left between plots, walled as yards or small gardens (C)

town_elements.name: animal pens (sheep, goats, donkeys)
town_elements.note: stockyard flocks (PF 58-60, A Darius-era) and donkeys fed bread (PFAT 0025 via POTTS2023, B); pens in the town, their walls (1.4 m) and dung floors C

town_elements.name: wells in squares and courts
town_elements.note: no qanat is dated to the Achaemenid period (Q-052): wells and river-fed canals only; well places and form C

town_elements.name: middens at the town edge, by the kiln and outside the stable
town_elements.note: SETTLEMENT.md zoning: middens by the kiln (C); ash, sherds, bone and dung where work happens (brief 5.5)

town_elements.name: domestic hearths, bread ovens, workshop forges and kilns
town_elements.note: 65 % of houses with a court hearth, 22 % with a bread oven (C); hearths lit as the light goes and banked a few hours after dark, relit before dawn; ovens before dawn; kilns and forges by day (fire.ts schedules, C); brief 9.2 'Fires are lit at dusk'

town_elements.name: storehouse of the royal stores
town_elements.note: PF 2-8: grain, flour and loaves taken to Persepolis 'for the royal stores' (A, Darius-era). No store excavated outside the Terrace (SETTLEMENT.md listed stores as not placed); placed here as C by the road south, magazines round a court (plan C) (D-043)

town_elements.name: state stable by the royal road
town_elements.note: horse rations for months at a time in 76 PF texts (POTTS2023, B); express couriers change horses at stations (HDT 8.98, B claim). No stable excavated (SETTLEMENT.md: not placed); placed C by the royal road W of the town, stalls on three sides of a yard (plan C) (D-043)

town_elements.name: plan of the ~1 ha official building N of the Terrace
town_elements.note: existence and size B/C (GONDET2018); plan (ranges of rooms round a court, a gate toward the Terrace, a square columned hall in the court, 6 m high) C

town_elements.name: Persepolis West Area B craft yard: kiln, bone pits, pigment workshop
town_elements.note: activity B (kiln, pits of bone fragments for the fluorapatite that whitened the Terrace limestone, pigment lumps incl. Egyptian blue made on site); walled yard 44 x 34 m, kiln form, pit form, furnace, grinding slabs, midden by the kiln C

town_elements.name: Persepolis West Area C garden: ditch grid in an enclosing wall
town_elements.note: 'a grid of ditches with a fencing wall, read as a garden' (PW2017, B); 170 x 130 m, 12 m ditch spacing, 2.4 m wall and fruit trees C

town_elements.name: walled garden behind the Tol-e Ajori gate
town_elements.note: Achaemenid garden complexes in the zone (GONDET2009, B); column bases and foundations beyond the gate (press, C). 330 x 260 m, the gate in its ESE wall, beds divided by stone-lined channels with basins after the Pasargadae garden (B analogy), cypress and plane on the axis, fruit trees in the beds (species B, mix C)

town_elements.name: walled garden at Dasht-e Gohar
town_elements.note: garden complexes in the zone (GONDET2009, B); 210 x 150 m E of Takht-e Rustam, channels and planting as the Bagh-e Firuzi garden (C)

town_elements.name: columned hall behind Takht-e Rustam
town_elements.note: 'a hypostyle hall reburied behind the platform' (search extract, C); 4 x 5 columns on stone bases, 24 x 30 m, flat roof, back wall: size and plan C

town_elements.name: elite estates: courtyard house, orchard, pool
town_elements.note: very low-density elite occupation among gardens (GONDET2009, B); estate households of 15-45 (population.json template, C); 90 x 70 m walled orchard with a 34 m courtyard house (C)

town_elements.name: walled orchards among the town blocks
town_elements.note: a garden city of separate blocks among gardens, parks, fields and orchards (SELOPERSE, B); orchard places, walls and plantings C

town_elements.name: plan of the way-station at the Kur crossing
town_elements.note: stations a day apart on the royal road (ROYALROAD-GIS, B); walled court 44 x 44 m with rooms, store and stable, well and hearth by analogy with the Jinjun and Qaleh-ye Kali stations (B analogy, C here); travel rations by the sealed document (HYLAND2022, B)

town_elements.name: spur from the royal road to the Tol-e Ajori gate
town_elements.note: course C

town_elements.name: Takht-e Rustam steps
town_elements.note: 12.5 x 12.5 m base and two steps (B size); step height 1.1 m and set-back 1.0 m not retrieved (C); orientation C

town_elements.name: two stone plinths of the sacred precinct
town_elements.note: after the Pasargadae precinct (search extracts, B form): white limestone on black limestone borders, 2.8 and 2.5 m square, 2 m high, ~9 m apart, the S one with a monolithic stair (eight or nine steps: Q-470); orientation (true N-S), the stair's side and the border's size C. Tier C (D-228): the form is B at Pasargadae; plinths at Persepolis, their place and orientation are an analogy (C, D-207, D-209); the file's rule is tier = the lower of existence and position.

town_elements.name: stepped fire altar with the kept fire
town_elements.note: form after the tomb reliefs at Naqsh-e Rustam (B: a stepped foot, a shaft, a stepped top); 0.9 m across, 1.18 m high, local limestone (C); the fire kept on it, its wood stacked by it and its ash heaped E (C)

town_elements.name: graves of the town's burial ground
town_elements.note: 140 low earth mounds in loose rows over single graves (Herodotus 1.140: the body coated in wax and buried in the earth, B claim; the form of the graves C), some ringed with a few field stones (C)

town_elements.name: house walls: mud brick on a fieldstone footing, mud plaster
town_elements.note: D-234: sun-dried brick (~33 cm, Iranica SX, B) two bricks and a render thick (0.7 m; 0.55 to the court, 0.4 between rooms; C); a footing of rough fieldstones 0.2-0.6 m above the lane (stone foundations under mud brick at Hasanlu, Baba Jan, Tall-i Takht: B analogues); straw-tempered mud plaster (Stein et al. 2016, B) with a renewed skirting coat, repairs, bare brick where it has fallen, soot above hearths (C); a niche by the street door, a drain hole to the lane (C)

town_elements.name: flat roofs: poplar poles, brush and matting, packed earth; eaves, lips and spouts; things kept on the roof
town_elements.note: D-234: poles spanning the 3-4 m rooms (the plan's room depth), brush and matting, 12 cm of earth with a clay-and-straw coat laid to a 2 % fall; the eave oversails the court 0.24-0.38 m on the pole ends with a mud lip; timber spouts (all C by analogy: Babylonian roofs of mud over matting on rafters, Hasanlu reed impressions: B analogues; the region's vernacular: C); a parapet by the household's standing (0.2-0.6 m, C); a stone roller (Iron Age roof rollers, SX: C), fuel, sleeping mats (C)

town_elements.name: ladders to the roofs
town_elements.note: D-234: a poplar ladder against a court facade in every house with a court (C: wooden stairways in Babylonian houses and brick stairs in the Hasanlu buildings are B analogues for larger buildings)

town_elements.name: porticoes of timber posts before the main room of large houses
town_elements.note: D-234: two timber posts on rough stone bases, a beam and a roof like the rooms' (paired wooden portico columns, uncarved stone bases: Hasanlu, B analogue; columned rooms on courts at Baba Jan and Nush-i Jan: B analogues); only in large houses (27 in the town, C)

town_elements.name: what households keep in their courts
town_elements.note: D-234 (the user's direction UD-08/UD-14, D-236): benches (Tol-e Ajori, Hasanlu: B analogues), the household's donkey, goats or sheep tied at a manger (PF animal rations, B; in the court C), fodder, brushwood and dung-cake fuel, baskets, a mortar, washing on a line, a fleece on the parapet, a cradle (C); each house by its own hash, none the same
